edges.description: Fragile perifollicular capillaries rupture around hair follicles, producing petechial and perifollicular hemorrhage.
Subcutaneous microvascular rupture causes confluent ecchymoses, especially over the lower extremities.
Gingival microvascular fragility and periodontal collagen breakdown cause friable, bleeding gums.
Cutaneous red blood cell extravasation and hemosiderin deposition produce skin discoloration.
Microvascular basement membrane and vessel wall damage cause pinpoint cutaneous hemorrhages (petechiae).
Synovial and periarticular microvascular hemorrhage (hemarthrosis) and connective tissue fragility produce painful joints.
Defective osteoid seam formation and subperiosteal/metaphyseal bone changes cause severe bone pain.
Impaired osteoblast osteoid matrix deposition reduces bone strength and increases fracture susceptibility.
Scorbutic bone matrix failure and subperiosteal pathology produce painful periostitis in infants, leading to pseudoparalysis of affected limbs.
Modified dentin formation and periodontal collagen breakdown cause loosening and premature loss of teeth.
edges.source: Defective Dentin and Periodontal Matrix Formation
